Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@bluebridge.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap + recommended evals / quant tradeoffs

Hi Xavier / Julia,

Thanks for the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and the things we promised to share so your engineering and MLOps teams can evaluate fit: 

1) Recommended baseline models for your use case (extraction + short-answer synthesis):
   - Llama2-13B (fp16) — best baseline accuracy for developer prompts we saw
   - Mixtral-8x7B (AWQ 4-bit) — competitive throughput with only small drop on named-entity recall in our tests
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP8 candidate) — faster inference, watch for hallucination on longer contexts

2) Why these: we prioritized models with strong entity/QA accuracy on your sample prompts and reasonable latency on our host configs. The attached prompt set (bluebridge_prompt_set_v1.txt) is the exact shard we used.

3) Quantization/throughput framing you asked about:
   - AWQ/GPTQ (4-bit) trades ~10–18% reduction in end-task F1 on entity extraction vs fp16 depending on model; throughput gains ~2.5–4x depending on batching.
   - FP8 (mixed-precision runtime) often gives smaller accuracy drops vs 4-bit but requires more recent kernel support (NVIDIA Hopper+ or Redwood FP8 path).
   - We included a short trade study PDF (redwood_awq_gptq_fp8_tradeoff_notes.pdf) summarizing per-model curves.

4) Benchmarks: I uploaded a start-to-finish bench report to the link below (includes token-level latency, end-to-end throughput, and cost projection).

5) Proposed next steps:
   - You: confirm which two models you want us to benchmark on your workload (suggest Llama2-13B fp16 + Mixtral-8x AWQ).
   - Us: run a focused run with your prompt shard and share a throughput matrix + recommended config (batch sizes, KV cache policy, and suggested quantization profile).
   - Schedule: technical deep-dive with Rishi and Connor next week (30–45m) to review regression mitigations and deployment options.

I attached the prompt set and the tradeoff summary. Will follow up internally for a technical commit.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Marissa / team / Xavier — quick technical notes and attached throughput matrix (xbrg_throughput_matrix_dec2026.csv). High level: 

1) Latency target & model choices:
   - Llama2-13B fp16 (single request, no batching) on A100/Hopper 80GB: 95p token-latency ~210–260ms for ~120-token inputs. Accuracy is highest of the options.
   - Mixtral-8x7B (AWQ 4-bit) on same hardware: 95p token-latency ~90–140ms; throughput jumps ~3x. Expect ~12% drop in entity F1 on your prompt shard (see attached CSV).
   - Mistral-7B FP8 candidate: 95p token-latency ~70–110ms on Hopper with FP8 kernels; accuracy varies — watch for ~6–10% precision drop in longer-context QA.

2) AWQ vs GPTQ specifics:
   - AWQ (our preferred 4-bit pipeline) gives denser kernels and better end-to-end memory efficiency. For Mixtral we observed AWQ slightly better on recall vs vanilla GPTQ at the same bitwidth in our evals.
   - GPTQ implementations vary; some models show worse recall on noun-entity extraction than AWQ. We recommend AWQ first for extraction-heavy workloads.

3) FP8 stability and canary guidance:
   - FP8 runtime on Redwood is production-ready for inference; caveat: we need to lock kernel versions and ensure customer VM images have the correct CUDA/cuDNN/MLA runtime. For a canary: run FP8 on a small dedicated Hopper pool with rollout to 5% traffic and a prompt-based regression monitor (we can provide).

4) KV cache / audit logs during evals:
   - For eval runs we can disable persistent KV retention and keep full request/response logs in a temporary bucket for 30 days (audit-friendly). We'll supply an export manifest for their SOC team.

5) Next steps (technical):
   - We will run two focused runs: Llama2-13B fp16 (baseline) and Mixtral-8x AWQ. Output: CSV with token-level latency quantiles, end-task precision/recall/F1 on Bluebridge prompt shard, and cost projection at 95p latency targets.
   - Connor: can you coordinate the cluster profile and make the run reproducible (image + kernel versions)?

I'll attach the throughput matrix and short PDF notes. Happy to jump on the call — I can do Monday 11a–1p PT.

Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML / Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
